newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians protest Israeli policies in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians protest Israeli policies in Jerusalem.

text.p: Palestinians demonstrated on Sunday outside the walls of Jerusalem's Old City and shops closed in an organised protest at Israeli tax raids in Arab East Jerusalem.
"(The policy) has weakened the economy of this city," said Faisal al-Husseini, in charge of Palestinian affairs in East Jerusalem.
"No services, no rights, no taxes," he said.

The protests are the Palestinians' latest weapons in an economic war they say Israel launched to drive them out of East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed in a move not recognised by the international community.

More than 100 Palestinians, led by Husseini, staged a protest sit-in on the steps of the Old City's Damascus Gate carrying banners and shouting slogans condemning Israeli measures against Arabs in the holy city.

"Israel's taxation policy means transfer" and "Confiscation of identification cards and closures are illegal", read the banners carried by demonstrators who shouted "God is Great" and "Jerusalem is the Palestinian Arab capital." Israeli soldiers and police stood above the protesters and watched.
"Israel can't force us to leave our land by their policies," shouted one demonstrator.
The usually crowded and busy narrow streets of East Jerusalem were empty. The shops were padlocked shut in observance of a general strike called by the Palestinian Chamber of Commerce.
Israeli officials, escorted by police, this month raided Palestinian shops in Arab East Jerusalem, and confiscated the property of those who could not pay their taxes.
The Israeli municipality of Jerusalem said the raids were conducted in both East Jerusalem and Jewish West Jerusalem and denied they were politically motivated.

"We are here protesting Israel's discrimination against Palestinians in Jerusalem. The people here are fed up with Israel's policies of totally sealing Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank which is destroying the city's economy," said Palestinian lawmaker Ziad Abu Zayyad.

"At the same time Israel is imposing many different and extremely high taxes and fees which people can't afford paying. This policy is also accompanied by measures aimed at reducing the numbers of Palestinians in Jerusalem and kicking them out of the city," he told reporters.

Palestinians complained Arab merchants were forced to pay taxes in excess of their business capital. They said in return, they received fewer and poorer services for taxes collected by the municipality than Jews living in the west side of the city.

Israel has clamped a closure on PLO-ruled self-areas, preventing Palestinians in the West Bank from entering Jerusalem. The closure has been imposed since the PLO's takeover of parts of the West Bank and Gaza beginning in 1994 and following suicide attacks by Moslem militants in Israel. The closure was eased but never lifted.

Near Deir al-Balah in the Gaza Strip, a senior PLO security official complained to Israel at the bulldozing of Arab-owned land recently seized by Jewish settlers despite an agreement to evacuate the site.
"We condemn this. It is a violation of the agreement...Even if this land is state land, they can't change its geographic features," said Brigadier General Abdel-Razek al-Majaideh.
